steps.name: Load, QC, and confirm design structure
caveats: Do not assume sample order in counts.csv matches metadata.csv row order — join explicitly on sample ID
12000 x 13 CSV includes the gene-symbol column as column 1; confirm it is excluded from the numeric count matrix before any arithmetic
steps.question: Do the raw counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata.csv (12 samples x condition, batch) match the profiled design of 6 treated vs 6 control with two batches balanced across condition, and are the counts suitable for DESeq2 (non-negative integers, no missing samples)?
constraints: Use the raw integer counts as provided; do not pre-normalize before DESeq2, which requires raw counts
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix loaded with gene symbols as row names and all 12 sample columns matching metadata sample IDs exactly
Cross-tabulation of condition x batch reported explicitly, confirming 3 treated + 3 control (or the actual observed split) per batch
Library size and gene-count distribution per sample reported; any sample with markedly divergent library size flagged
Genes with zero counts across all samples identified and reported (not yet filtered, filtering happens in DESeq2 step)

steps.name: Batch-adjusted differential expression: treated vs control
caveats: With n=6 per group and only two batches, do not additionally attempt a batch:condition interaction term — there is no power to estimate it; batch is included only as an additive covariate
Use apeglm or ashr shrinkage (not the default normal shrinkage) for log2FoldChange reporting used in the volcano/MA plots to avoid inflated fold changes for low-count genes

12000 input genes is a pre-filtered/reduced gene set (not whole-transcriptome ~20k+); do not apply additional aggressive low-count filtering beyond DESeq2 defaults, or too few genes may remain testable
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples when batch (two known processing batches) is included as a covariate in the model?
constraints: Design formula must be ~ batch + condition, not ~ condition alone, since batch is a known confounder even though it is balanced
Report both raw and BH-adjusted p-values for the full gene list, not only the significant subset
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run with design ~ batch + condition on raw integer counts, condition releveled so control is the reference level
Treated-vs-control contrast extracted with independent filtering (default alpha=0.05) and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction
Results table reports gene symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj for all tested genes, sorted by padj
Significant gene list defined at padj < 0.05 (report count of significant genes; if fewer than 10 genes are significant, state this as a low-power finding rather than reinterpreting the threshold)
PCA plot of variance-stabilized (vst) counts colored by condition and shaped by batch produced, to visually confirm batch is a secondary axis of variation relative to condition
MA plot and a volcano plot of the treated-vs-control contrast produced
Dispersion estimates plot produced to confirm model fit is reasonable for this sample size

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the treated-vs-control gene signature
caveats: Gene symbol casing/format in the WikiPathways GMT (HGNC) must match the counts.csv gene symbol column; normalize case before matching
The GMT's first field is '%'-delimited (name, WikiPathways ID, species) and must be split to obtain a readable pathway name before reporting
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples (batch-adjusted DESeq2 result)?
constraints: Do not use a non-human WikiPathways GMT (rat/mouse) as a substitute for missing human data
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run separately for up-regulated (positive log2FC, padj<0.05) and down-regulated (negative log2FC, padj<0.05) significant genes against the full tested gene list as background

If the significant gene count from T1S2 is very small (e.g., <15 genes per direction), report this explicitly and additionally run a pre-ranked GSEA using the full DESeq2 stat column against WikiPathways human gene sets as a more powered complement

Pathway gene sets are the WikiPathways human GMT resolved from the environment's reference store at run time; if the resource is unexpectedly absent, report the gap rather than substituting a different-species pathway set
Output table includes pathway name, WikiPathways ID, overlap size, gene ratio, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value, sorted by adjusted p-value
Top enriched pathways (adjusted p<0.05, or top 20 by p-value if none pass FDR) reported with the member DE genes driving each

plan.title: Batch-adjusted DESeq2 DE: treated vs control kidney
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is a clean 2x2: 12 kidney samples, 6 treated vs 6 control, with two known processing batches balanced across conditions (i.e., batch is not confounded with condition). This is the textbook case for a paired-factor design in DESeq2 using ~batch + condition, which removes batch-driven variance from the model without needing an empirical batch-correction tool like ComBat/SVA (those are for when batch structure is unknown or unbalanced — here it is known and balanced, so modeling it directly is more appropriate and preserves valid inference). The pipeline is: (1) load and QC the raw counts/metadata, confirm the 6v6 balanced-batch structure exactly as profiled; (2) run DESeq2 with the batch-adjusted design, extract the treated-vs-control contrast with independent filtering and a fixed FDR threshold, and produce standard diagnostic and result visualizations; (3) take the resulting significant gene list into WikiPathways human pathway enrichment to give the DE signature biological context. Each step operates on a single primary data object (count matrix -> DESeq2 results -> gene list -> pathway enrichment) and is routed to the matching agent.
